name: OpenText Cloud Platform
scope_notes: Covers OpenText Cloud Platform (Admin Center / Thrust Services APIs, used by OpenText Core SaaS apps such as Core Content). Covers the OAuth service clients and tokens of OpenText Cloud Platform (formerly OT2 / Developer Cloud), which back Core Content and other Core SaaS APIs at <region>.api.opentext.com; on-prem Content Server/OTDS and Admin Center help (CDAC-H-*) pages are not covered.

controls.name: Revoke client
controls.what: Revokes access tokens for a confidential service client.
controls.setting: Admin Center > Service clients > More options > Revoke client

controls.name: Regenerate client
controls.what: Issues a new client secret for a confidential client.
controls.setting: Admin Center > Service clients > More options > Regenerate client

controls.name: Edit token lifetimes
controls.what: Sets access (900-28800 s) and refresh (900 s-1 year) token lifetimes per client.
controls.setting: Admin Center > Service clients > More options > Edit token lifetimes; Admin API Client.accessTokenLifetime / refreshTokenLifetime

controls.name: Deactivate service client (activate=false)
controls.what: Deactivates an app or organization service client through the Admin API.

controls.name: Client level (organization / tenant / app)
controls.what: Choosing an app-level client limits access to one application instead of the whole tenant or organization.
controls.setting: Admin Center > Integrations > Service Clients at tenant or app level

controls.name: allowedScopes
controls.what: Lists the scopes a client may request.

controls.name: Tenant Admin role on service client
controls.what: Controls whether a tenant service client gets the Tenant administrator role.
controls.setting: Tenant > Integration > Service Clients > Add > Tenant Admin role

controls.name: Redirect URLs
controls.what: Only registered redirect URLs can receive authorization codes.
controls.setting: Admin Center > Service clients > Redirect URLs

no_control.what: Public clients cannot be revoked or regenerated in Admin Center (only confidential clients can).

controls_unknown: Audit log for OpenText Cloud Platform / Admin Center: event names for client create, regenerate, revoke and token issuance; retention; how to export.
Whether API calls or data reads (e.g. Core Content GET /v3/files) are logged and which field identifies the client.
Whether client secrets expire or can be given an expiry.
Any IP/network restriction on service clients or tokens.
Whether 'Revoke client' invalidates already-issued access tokens immediately, and whether it also invalidates the secret.
Default token lifetimes when not edited (Core Capture sample shows 900 s).
Whether the password grant can be disabled per tenant, and whether IdP MFA applies to it.

credentials.name: Confidential service client (organization, extension app, tenant-level or app-level) - client credentials

authentication.summary: Admin Center creates confidential OAuth clients at organization, tenant or app level (and for each extension app of a Core SaaS app such as Core Content). The holder posts client_id and client_secret to https://<region>.api.opentext.com/tenants/<tenant>/oauth2/token (or the organizations/... endpoint) and gets a bearer token.

federation.details: Client credentials carry no user, so no IdP sign-in occurs. The docs do not say how SSO or conditional access policies relate to service clients.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP allowlist for service clients or tokens found in the developer docs or Admin API spec.

lifetime.summary: Access token 900-28800 s per client; secret expiry not documented

renewal.summary: Client requests a new token with the same secret; secret changes only when an admin regenerates it.

administration.summary: Organization-level clients are created by the OpenText Developer Admin, tenant-level by tenant admins, app-level by app admins. Tenant-level clients reach all applications in the tenant and can be assigned the Tenant administrator role (used for SCIM).
administration.conditions: Every new or extended app gets a client pair automatically.

offboard.details: Service clients belong to the organization (or app/tenant), not to a user.

inventory.details: Admin Center > Service clients page lists the clients; the Admin API has GET /organizations/{organizationId}/clients (Get service clients).

token_format.notes: Opaque bearer token per docs; format not documented.

anomaly_cues: Tenant-level clients with Tenant administrator role
Organization-level clients used against many tenants
Secret regenerations not tied to change tickets

containment.steps: Admin Center > Service clients > Revoke client, then Regenerate client; or PATCH the client with activate=false.
containment.notes: Docs say Revoke client revokes an access token but do not state scope or timing.

unknown: Audit event names and log location

calls.reveals: Whether the client works and its token
All tenant users (organization client via Admin API)

credentials.name: Resource owner password grant (confidential client + user name/password)

authentication.summary: A confidential client sends its secret plus a user's name and password to the tenant token endpoint and receives access and refresh tokens in that user's context. OpenText says this is for testing only.

federation.details: The password is sent straight to the OpenText token endpoint; the docs do not say whether federated IdP MFA or policies apply or whether the grant can be turned off.

lifetime.summary: Access 900-28800 s; refresh up to 1 year

renewal.summary: Refresh tokens are single-use and replaced on each refresh.

administration.summary: No admin setting to disable the password grant was found; OpenText only advises against production use. Organizations also have a service account password managed in Admin Center.

token_format.notes: Opaque bearer token per docs; format not documented.

anomaly_cues: Same client used with many user names

containment.steps: Revoke the confidential client; reset the user's password.
containment.notes: Docs say Revoke client revokes an access token but do not state scope or timing.

unknown: Audit event names and log location

calls.reveals: Access and refresh token for the user

credentials.name: User access/refresh tokens via authorization code (confidential) or PKCE (public client)

authentication.summary: Users sign in through the tenant oauth2/auth endpoint (and the tenant's authentication handler, e.g. SAML to Okta/Google), and the app exchanges the code for access, refresh and ID tokens. Public clients use PKCE and have no secret.

federation.details: The interactive sign-in goes through the tenant's configured authentication scheme (e.g. SAML IdP). Whether refresh tokens are re-checked against the IdP is not documented.

lifetime.summary: Refresh token up to 1 year; access 900-28800 s

administration.summary: Redirect URLs must be registered per client (up to three for tenant clients). Revoke client and Regenerate exist only for confidential clients; public clients can be deactivated via the Admin API.

token_format.notes: Opaque bearer token per docs; format not documented.

anomaly_cues: Long refresh token lifetimes (up to 1 year)

containment.steps: Revoke the confidential client; for public clients deactivate via Admin API activate=false; disable the user.
containment.notes: Docs say Revoke client revokes an access token but do not state scope or timing.
